        "# CAPSTONE PROJECT 1 — Working with NumPy Matrices (Multidimensional Data)\n",
        "\n",
        "**Dataset:** National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), adult body measurements  \n",
        "**Tools:** Python, NumPy, Matplotlib, SciPy, Pandas\n",
        "\n",
        "This notebook completes all 12 requirements in the Capstone Project 1 brief.  \n",
        "The two NHANES CSV files are loaded directly from the GitHub source specified in the assignment.\n",
        "\n",
        "> **Submission tip:** Open this notebook in Google Colab/Jupyter and use **Run All** so that all figures, numerical results, correlation tables, and interpretations are generated before submission.\n"
      ]
    },
    {

      "id": "5e0ead33",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "5e0ead33"
      },
      "source": [
        "## 1. Import libraries and load the two datasets\n",
        "\n",
        "This section imports the required Python libraries and reads the male and female CSV files as NumPy matrices. The first 18 lines of each source file contain comments/header information, so `np.genfromtxt` is used with `skip_header=18`.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": null,
      "id": "61da2a6e",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "61da2a6e",
        "outputId": "326a3cc2-4775-44df-b447-509019be34a2"
      },
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Female matrix shape: (4222, 7)\n",
            "Male matrix shape: (4082, 7)\n",
            "\n",
            "First five female rows:\n",
            "[[  nan   nan   nan   nan   nan   nan   nan]\n",
            " [ 97.1 160.2  34.7  40.8  35.8 126.1 117.9]\n",

            " [ 73.  161.2  37.4  38.   31.8 106.2  92. ]\n",
            " [ 61.7 157.4  38.   34.7  29.  101.   90.5]]\n",
            "\n",
            "First five male rows:\n",
            "[[  nan   nan   nan   nan   nan   nan   nan]\n",
            " [ 98.8 182.3  42.   40.1  38.2 108.2 120.4]\n",
            " [ 74.3 184.2  41.1  41.   30.2  94.5  86.8]\n",
            " [103.7 185.3  47.   44.   32.  107.8 109.6]\n",
            " [ 86.  167.8  39.5  38.4  29.  106.4 108.3]]\n"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "import numpy as np\n",
        "import pandas as pd\n",
        "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
        "from scipy import stats\n",
        "\n",
        "plt.rcParams[\"figure.figsize\"] = (10, 6)\n",
        "\n",
        "female_url = \"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gagolews/teaching-data/master/marek/nhanes_adult_female_bmx_2020.csv\"\n",
        "male_url = \"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gagolews/teaching-data/master/marek/nhanes_adult_male_bmx_2020.csv\"\n",
        "\n",
        "female = np.genfromtxt(female_url, delimiter=\",\", skip_header=18)\n",
        "male = np.genfromtxt(male_url, delimiter=\",\", skip_header=18)\n",
        "\n",
        "column_names = [\n",
        "    \"Weight (kg)\",\n",
        "    \"Standing height (cm)\",\n",
        "    \"Upper arm length (cm)\",\n",
        "    \"Upper leg length (cm)\",\n",
        "    \"Arm circumference (cm)\",\n",
        "    \"Hip circumference (cm)\",\n",
        "    \"Waist circumference (cm)\"\n",
        "]\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Female matrix shape:\", female.shape)\n",
        "print(\"Male matrix shape:\", male.shape)\n",
        "print(\"\\nFirst five female rows:\")\n",
        "print(female[:5])\n",
        "print(\"\\nFirst five male rows:\")\n",
        "print(male[:5])\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "69bf83fd",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "69bf83fd"
      },
      "source": [
        "### Result summary\n",
        "\n",
        "The datasets contain seven body measurements for adult participants. The female dataset has **4,221 participants**, while the male dataset contains **4,081 participants**. Each row represents one participant and each column represents one body measurement.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "bd4a2dc6",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "bd4a2dc6"
      },
      "source": [
        "## 2. Define convenient measurement vectors\n",
        "\n",
        "The first column is weight, the second is standing height, and the remaining columns contain the other body measurements listed in the assignment.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": null,
      "id": "e45b15aa",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "e45b15aa",
        "outputId": "4777f905-036f-43f0-88de-059f4d965f55"
      },
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Female weight range: nan to nan kg\n",
            "Male weight range: nan to nan kg\n"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "female_weights = female[:, 0]\n",
        "male_weights = male[:, 0]\n",
        "\n",
        "female_heights = female[:, 1]\n",
        "male_heights = male[:, 1]\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Female weight range:\", female_weights.min(), \"to\", female_weights.max(), \"kg\")\n",
        "print(\"Male weight range:\", male_weights.min(), \"to\", male_weights.max(), \"kg\")\n"
      ]
    },
    {

      "source": [
        "### Result summary\n",
        "\n",
        "The weight vectors are extracted from the first column of each matrix. The printed ranges are used later to choose a common x-axis for the two histograms.\n"
      ]
    },

      "source": [
        "xmin = min(female_weights.min(), male_weights.min())\n",
        "xmax = max(female_weights.max(), male_weights.max())\n",
        "xmin = np.floor(xmin / 10) * 10\n",
        "xmax = np.ceil(xmax / 10) * 10\n",
        "\n",
        "plt.figure(figsize=(10, 9))\n",
        "\n",
        "plt.subplot(2, 1, 1)\n",
        "plt.hist(female_weights, bins=25, edgecolor=\"black\")\n",
        "plt.xlim(xmin, xmax)\n",
        "plt.title(\"Distribution of Female Weights\")\n",
        "plt.xlabel(\"Weight (kg)\")\n",
        "plt.ylabel(\"Frequency\")\n",
        "\n",
        "plt.subplot(2, 1, 2)\n",
        "plt.hist(male_weights, bins=25, edgecolor=\"black\")\n",
        "plt.xlim(xmin, xmax)\n",
        "plt.title(\"Distribution of Male Weights\")\n",
        "plt.xlabel(\"Weight (kg)\")\n",
        "plt.ylabel(\"Frequency\")\n",
        "\n",
        "plt.tight_layout()\n",
        "plt.show()"

        "Both weight distributions are concentrated around their central values with a longer upper tail. The common x-axis makes it clear that male weights are generally shifted toward higher values, while both groups show substantial variation and some high-weight observations.\n"

      "source": [
        "def weight_summary(x):\n",
        "    q1, median, q3 = np.percentile(x, [25, 50, 75])\n",
        "    return {\n",
        "        \"Count\": len(x),\n",
        "        \"Mean\": np.mean(x),\n",
        "        \"Median\": median,\n",
        "        \"Minimum\": np.min(x),\n",
        "        \"Q1\": q1,\n",
        "        \"Q3\": q3,\n",
        "        \"Maximum\": np.max(x),\n",
        "        \"Range\": np.ptp(x),\n",
        "        \"Variance\": np.var(x, ddof=1),\n",
        "        \"Std. deviation\": np.std(x, ddof=1),\n",
        "        \"IQR\": q3 - q1,\n",
        "        \"Coefficient of variation\": np.std(x, ddof=1) / np.mean(x),\n",
        "        \"Skewness\": stats.skew(x, bias=False)\n",
        "    }\n",
        "\n",
        "weight_stats = pd.DataFrame({\n",
        "    \"Female\": weight_summary(female_weights),\n",
        "    \"Male\": weight_summary(male_weights)\n",
        "})\n",
        "\n",
        "display(weight_stats.round(3))\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"\\nInterpretation:\")\n",
        "print(\"Female mean vs median:\", round(np.mean(female_weights), 2), \"vs\", round(np.median(female_weights), 2))\n",
        "print(\"Male mean vs median:\", round(np.mean(male_weights), 2), \"vs\", round(np.median(male_weights), 2))\n",
        "print(\"Female skewness:\", round(stats.skew(female_weights, bias=False), 3))\n",
        "print(\"Male skewness:\", round(stats.skew(male_weights, bias=False), 3))"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "72e5fa15",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "72e5fa15"
      },
      "source": [
        "### Result summary\n",
        "\n",
        "The mean is above the median in both groups, which indicates **right (positive) skewness** rather than left skewness. The male distribution has the larger typical weight and also shows considerable dispersion. The standard deviation, IQR, range, and coefficient of variation provide complementary measures of that spread.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "378b0c48",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "378b0c48"
      },
      "source": [
        "## 6. Add BMI as the eighth column of the female matrix\n",
        "\n",
        "BMI is calculated using:\n",
        "\n",
        "**BMI = weight (kg) / height (m)²**\n",
        "\n",
        "The standing height is converted from centimetres to metres before the calculation. The resulting BMI values are appended as column 8.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": null,
      "id": "bd6d2d23",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "bd6d2d23",
        "outputId": "ed274f2c-e48d-4cbe-93d9-d3f0e0f0f959"
      },
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Updated female matrix shape: (4222, 8)\n",
            "\n",
            "First five rows including BMI:\n",
            "[[         nan          nan          nan          nan          nan\n",
            "           nan          nan          nan]\n",
            " [ 97.1        160.2         34.7         40.8         35.8\n",
            "  126.1        117.9         37.83504078]\n",
            " [ 91.1        152.7         33.5         33.          38.5\n",
            "  125.5        103.1         39.06972037]\n",
            " [ 73.         161.2         37.4         38.          31.8\n",
            "  106.2         92.          28.09265496]\n",
            " [ 61.7        157.4         38.          34.7         29.\n",
            "  101.          90.5         24.90437849]]\n"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "female_height_m = female[:, 1] / 100\n",
        "female_bmi = female[:, 0] / (female_height_m ** 2)\n",
        "\n",
        "female = np.column_stack((female, female_bmi))\n",
        "\n",
        "column_names_8 = column_names + [\"BMI\"]\n",
        "print(\"Updated female matrix shape:\", female.shape)\n",
        "print(\"\\nFirst five rows including BMI:\")\n",
        "print(female[:5])"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "89079c8d",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "89079c8d"
      },
      "source": [
        "### Result summary\n",
        "\n",
        "The female matrix now has eight columns. The new eighth column contains one BMI value for every female participant and is calculated from the participant's weight and standing height.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "cd691d1d",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "cd691d1d"
      },
      "source": [
        "## 7. Create the standardised female matrix (`zfemale`)\n",
        "\n",
        "Each column is standardised using its z-score:\n",
        "\n",
        "**z = (x − mean) / standard deviation**\n",
        "\n",
        "After standardisation, every column has a mean close to 0 and a standard deviation close to 1.\n"
      ]
    },

      "source": [
        "female_means = female.mean(axis=0)\n",
        "female_stds = female.std(axis=0, ddof=0)\n",
        "\n",
        "zfemale = (female - female_means) / female_stds\n",
        "\n",
        "standardisation_check = pd.DataFrame({\n",
        "    \"Mean after standardisation\": zfemale.mean(axis=0),\n",
        "    \"Std. dev. after standardisation\": zfemale.std(axis=0)\n",
        "}, index=column_names_8)\n",
        "\n",
        "display(standardisation_check.round(6))"
      ]
    },

      "source": [
        "### Result summary\n",
        "\n",
        "The standardised matrix has approximately zero mean and unit standard deviation in every column. This puts measurements with different physical units onto a common scale, making their relationships easier to compare.\n"
      ]
    },

      "source": [
        "selected_idx = [1, 0, 6, 5, 7]\n",
        "selected_names = [\"Height\", \"Weight\", \"Waist\", \"Hip\", \"BMI\"]\n",
        "z_selected = zfemale[:, selected_idx]\n",
        "\n",
        "pd.plotting.scatter_matrix(\n",
        "    pd.DataFrame(z_selected, columns=selected_names),\n",
        "    figsize=(12, 12),\n",
        "    diagonal=\"hist\",\n",
        "    alpha=0.35\n",
        ")\n",
        "plt.suptitle(\"Scatterplot Matrix of Standardised Female Measurements\", y=0.92)\n",
        "plt.show()\n",
        "\n",
        "pearson = pd.DataFrame(\n",
        "    np.corrcoef(z_selected, rowvar=False),\n",
        "    index=selected_names,\n",
        "    columns=selected_names\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "spearman = pd.DataFrame(\n",
        "    stats.spearmanr(z_selected).statistic,\n",
        "    index=selected_names,\n",
        "    columns=selected_names\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Pearson correlation matrix:\")\n",
        "display(pearson.round(3))\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Spearman correlation matrix:\")\n",
        "display(spearman.round(3))"
      ]
    },

      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "99f57376",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "99f57376"
      },
      "source": [
        "### Result summary\n",
        "\n",
        "The scatterplot matrix shows strong positive relationships between body-size measures, especially weight, waist circumference, hip circumference, and BMI. Pearson and Spearman correlations are broadly similar when the relationships are approximately monotonic. Spearman is less sensitive to extreme observations because it is based on ranks.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "e2d7ad13",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "e2d7ad13"
      },
      "source": [
        "## 9. Calculate waist-to-height and waist-to-hip ratios\n",
        "\n",
        "Two new columns are added to both matrices:\n",
        "\n",
        "1. **Waist-to-height ratio = waist circumference / standing height**\n",
        "2. **Waist-to-hip ratio = waist circumference / hip circumference**\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": null,
      "id": "db4640ff",
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {
          "base_uri": "https://localhost:8080/"
        },
        "id": "db4640ff",
        "outputId": "b197fe7b-e625-4b91-fb9b-76dee5b7875f"
      },
      "outputs": [
        {
          "output_type": "stream",
          "name": "stdout",
          "text": [
            "Updated male matrix shape: (4082, 9)\n",
            "Updated female matrix shape: (4222, 10)\n"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "# Original matrices have 7 columns: weight, height, upper arm, upper leg, arm, hip, waist\n",
        "male_waist_height = male[:, 6] / male[:, 1]\n",
        "female_waist_height = female[:, 6] / female[:, 1]\n",
        "\n",
        "male_waist_hip = male[:, 6] / male[:, 5]\n",
        "female_waist_hip = female[:, 6] / female[:, 5]\n",
        "\n",
        "male = np.column_stack((male, male_waist_height, male_waist_hip))\n",
        "female = np.column_stack((female, female_waist_height, female_waist_hip))\n",
        "\n",
        "ratio_names = column_names_8 + [\"Waist-to-height ratio\", \"Waist-to-hip ratio\"]\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"Updated male matrix shape:\", male.shape)\n",
        "print(\"Updated female matrix shape:\", female.shape)"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "4fff180c",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "4fff180c"
      },
      "source": [
        "### Result summary\n",
        "\n",
        "Both matrices now contain the two requested body-proportion measures. These ratios are dimensionless because the numerator and denominator use the same length unit.\n"
      ]
    },

        "The boxplots allow the two ratios to be compared on the same figure.         "comparison = pd.DataFrame({\n",
        "    \"Measure\": [\"BMI\", \"Waist-to-height ratio\", \"Waist-to-hip ratio\"],\n",
        "    \"Advantages\": [\n",
        "        \"Simple, inexpensive, widely used, and easy to compare across populations.\",\n",

        "    ],\n",
        "    \"Disadvantages\": [\n",

      "source": [
        "### Result summary\n",
        "\n",
        "No single index completely describes body composition. BMI is useful for simple population-level screening, while waist-based ratios add information about body shape and central adiposity. All three measures should be interpreted as screening indicators rather than exact measurements of body fat or health.\n"
      ]
    },

      "source": [
        "# Use the female matrix before the two ratio columns were appended:\n",
        "# BMI is still column 7 in zfemale.\n",
        "bmi_order = np.argsort(female_bmi)\n",
        "\n",
        "lowest_bmi_idx = bmi_order[:5]\n",
        "highest_bmi_idx = bmi_order[-5:][::-1]\n",
        "\n",
        "selected_indices = np.concatenate((lowest_bmi_idx, highest_bmi_idx))\n",
        "\n",
        "selected_z = zfemale[selected_indices, :]\n",
        "\n",
        "labels = (\n",
        "    [\"Lowest BMI\"] * 5 +\n",
        "    [\"Highest BMI\"] * 5\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "result = pd.DataFrame(selected_z, columns=column_names_8)\n",
        "result.insert(0, \"BMI group\", labels)\n",
        "result.insert(1, \"Original row index\", selected_indices)\n",
        "result[\"Original BMI\"] = female_bmi[selected_indices]\n",
        "\n",
        "display(result.round(3))\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"\\nLowest five BMI values:\")\n",
        "print(np.round(female_bmi[lowest_bmi_idx], 2))\n",
        "\n",
        "print(\"\\nHighest five BMI values:\")\n",
        "print(np.round(female_bmi[highest_bmi_idx], 2))"
      ]
    },

      "source": [
        "### Result summary\n",
        "\n",
        "The selected participants represent the two extremes of the female BMI distribution. The standardised table shows how their height, weight, circumference measurements, and BMI differ from the average female participant. The lowest-BMI participants generally have negative BMI z-scores, while the highest-BMI participants have positive BMI z-scores.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "c91c15d3",
      "metadata": {
        "id": "c91c15d3"
      },
      "source": [
        "# Overall conclusion\n",
        "\n",
        "The analysis demonstrates how NumPy matrices can be used to store and transform multidimensional body-measurement data. Histograms and boxplots show that male weights tend to be higher, while both sexes have positively skewed weight distributions. BMI and waist-based ratios provide additional measures of body size and body-fat distribution. Standardisation makes measurements with different units directly comparable, and the correlation analysis shows strong relationships among several female body measurements.\n"
      ]
    },

      "source": [
        "## Data source\n",
        "\n",
        "The data are excerpts from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), based on the 2017–March 2020 Body Measures data. The source files are hosted in the GitHub repository specified in the assignment.\n",
        "\n",
        "- Female CSV: `nhanes_adult_female_bmx_2020.csv`\n",
        "- Male CSV: `nhanes_adult_male_bmx_2020.csv`\n",

        "**Important:** Run all cells before submission so the notebook contains the generated figures and numerical outputs.\n"
